- **Applied:** 0 dispatched (0 APPLIED, 0 other verdict)

## Conceptual correctness — fix these first

Unsound or contradictory concepts in the plan's design — the highest-priority gaps, addressed before the completeness gaps below. The audit reports these but does not apply them (read-only-audit split, #85): the paired apply verb walks them first, before the completeness gaps. Address them with:

    plan-tool completeness-apply telemetry-linkage-backfill   # walk + apply each correctness gap, then the completeness gaps
    plan-tool reconcile-plan-walk telemetry-linkage-backfill  # alternative interactive review/apply

- HIGH `[apply-verdict-anchor]`: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) drops the finding `anchor` the plan body requires on the apply-verdict event. Architecture Part B(2) and Acceptance criteria both promise "with the finding `anchor` slug + its `step_id` … + `plan_fingerprint`" / "with anchor + step_id + `plan_fingerprint`", but the detail's `record_apply_verdict(..., verdict, step_id, plan_fingerprint, code_fingerprint)` and its `context={"verdict", "step_id"}` carry no anchor at all. The constraint that resolves it: `apply_finding`'s params are `finding_body` + `step_id` (no anchor in scope); only the walk caller (`cli/review_actions.py`, `rec.anchor`) holds it, so recording *inside* `apply_finding` cannot carry the anchor without threading it in. This matters doubly because `_compute_decision_id` folds only `step_id` (not anchor/context), so multiple plan-wide findings that resolve to the same current/next-runnable step in the same second get identical `decision_id`s — the anchor is the *only* per-finding discriminator, and it is the join key the whole plan exists to populate.
- HIGH `[apply-verdict-code-fingerprint]`: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) carries the full `code_fingerprint` map, directly contradicting the body's repeated plan_fingerprint-only decision. The detail's Implementation says "Carry both fingerprints. … `code_fingerprint` is cheap here because the `Plan` is already parsed, so carry it too" and computes it via `compute_code_fingerprint`, but Ground rule 3 states "the per-finding apply-verdict site carries `plan_fingerprint` only", the Risks entry mitigates with "`plan_fingerprint`-only on the per-finding site", the Deferred section defers the full map, and Acceptance criteria assert "the per-finding apply site carries no full `code_fingerprint` map." Because `apply_finding` runs once per finding in the walk loop and step 4 computes the fingerprint *inside* it, this also re-hashes the code footprint per finding — the exact cost the "Line-volume / cost at hot sites" risk names — violating the "fingerprint compute is hoisted above per-finding loops" criterion. The body is authoritative (stated in four places with rationale).
- MEDIUM `[escalate-split-code-fingerprint]`: Step 5 (`05-record-escalate-split-outcome-decision`) carries both fingerprints while the body scopes escalate-split to `plan_fingerprint` only. Architecture Part B(3) and Acceptance criteria say the escalate-split event records "with the target `step_id` + `plan_fingerprint`" (Ground rule 3 reserves the full `code_fingerprint` map for "the drift-gate, and Part-A recorders that already have it cheaply"), but the detail's Implementation says "Carry both fingerprints … `code_fingerprint` … free here because `plan` is already parsed." Escalate fires rarely (per structural finding), so there is no volume harm, but the carry set diverges from the body with no bridge and the escalate decision is about plan *structure*/safety, not code footprint.
- MEDIUM `[create-plan-fingerprint-timing]`: Acceptance criterion 1 promises "a non-empty `plan_fingerprint`" at all six backfilled sites including create ×2, but step 2 (`02-...create.py...`) establishes that both create recorders fire inside `_review_step_change_types` **before** `write_new_plan`, so `compute_plan_fingerprint` has no file to read and returns empty there — the create sites can only carry a real `code_fingerprint`. The criterion is unsatisfiable as written.
- MEDIUM `[fingerprint-hoist]`: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) computes both fingerprints *inside* `apply_finding`, at the `parse_apply_verdict` consumption site (`launcher.py:2969`) — but `apply_finding` is invoked once per finding by the review/reconcile apply walk (`cli/review_actions.py:534`, inside the per-rec loop), so the compute runs per finding, directly contradicting ground-rule 4 ("compute the plan-state fingerprint once per apply/reconcile pass and reuse it across per-finding records, never recomputing inside the loop") and acceptance criterion "fingerprint compute is hoisted above per-finding loops." The constraint that resolves it: `apply_finding` is the single consumption point of `parse_apply_verdict` shared by six callers, so hoisting is foreclosed unless a precomputed digest is threaded through `apply_finding`'s signature; step 5 (`05-record-escalate-split-outcome-decision`) has the same shape (compute per `escalate_to_split` call, i.e. per structural finding), at lower frequency.

This matters doubly because `_compute_decision_id` folds only `step_id` (not anchor/context), so multiple plan-wide findings that resolve to the same current/next-runnable step in the same second get identical `decision_id`s — the anchor is the *only* per-finding discriminator, and it is the join key the whole plan exists to populate.
recommendations.suggested_action: specify that the apply-verdict record carries the finding anchor by recording where the `rec` is in scope (the walk caller) or by threading `rec.anchor` into the `apply_finding` site, and reflect that in step 4's tests.

recommendations.title: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) carries the full `code_fingerprint` map, directly contradicting the body'
recommendations.body: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) carries the full `code_fingerprint` map, directly contradicting the body's repeated plan_fingerprint-only decision. The detail's Implementation says "Carry both fingerprints. … `code_fingerprint` is cheap here because the `Plan` is already parsed, so carry it too" and computes it via `compute_code_fingerprint`, but Ground rule 3 states "the per-finding apply-verdict site carries `plan_fingerprint` only", the Risks entry mitigates with "`plan_fingerprint`-only on the per-finding site", the Deferred section defers the full map, and Acceptance criteria assert "the per-finding apply site carries no full `code_fingerprint` map." Because `apply_finding` runs once per finding in the walk loop and step 4 computes the fingerprint *inside* it, this also re-hashes the code footprint per finding — the exact cost the "Line-volume / cost at hot sites" risk names — violating the "fingerprint compute is hoisted above per-finding loops" criterion. The body is authoritative (stated in four places with rationale).
recommendations.suggested_action: correct step 4 to carry `plan_fingerprint` only and specify computing it once per apply/reconcile pass rather than inside the per-finding call.

recommendations.title: Step 5 (`05-record-escalate-split-outcome-decision`) carries both fingerprints while the body scopes escalate-split to `
recommendations.body: Step 5 (`05-record-escalate-split-outcome-decision`) carries both fingerprints while the body scopes escalate-split to `plan_fingerprint` only. Architecture Part B(3) and Acceptance criteria say the escalate-split event records "with the target `step_id` + `plan_fingerprint`" (Ground rule 3 reserves the full `code_fingerprint` map for "the drift-gate, and Part-A recorders that already have it cheaply"), but the detail's Implementation says "Carry both fingerprints … `code_fingerprint` … free here because `plan` is already parsed." Escalate fires rarely (per structural finding), so there is no volume harm, but the carry set diverges from the body with no bridge and the escalate decision is about plan *structure*/safety, not code footprint.
recommendations.suggested_action: reconcile the carry set — either bless `code_fingerprint` on escalate-split in the body's Part-B(3) rule and acceptance criterion, or drop it in step 5 to match the stated `plan_fingerprint`-only design.

recommendations.title: Acceptance criterion 1 promises "a non-empty `plan_fingerprint`" at all six backfilled sites including create ×2, but st
recommendations.body: Acceptance criterion 1 promises "a non-empty `plan_fingerprint`" at all six backfilled sites including create ×2, but step 2 (`02-...create.py...`) establishes that both create recorders fire inside `_review_step_change_types` **before** `write_new_plan`, so `compute_plan_fingerprint` has no file to read and returns empty there — the create sites can only carry a real `code_fingerprint`. The criterion is unsatisfiable as written.
recommendations.suggested_action: step 2's pre-write timing is the more-detailed decision — narrow acceptance criterion 1 so the two create sites are asserted on `code_fingerprint`, not `plan_fingerprint`.

recommendations.title: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) computes both fingerprints *inside* `apply_finding`, at the `parse_apply_
recommendations.body: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) computes both fingerprints *inside* `apply_finding`, at the `parse_apply_verdict` consumption site (`launcher.py:2969`) — but `apply_finding` is invoked once per finding by the review/reconcile apply walk (`cli/review_actions.py:534`, inside the per-rec loop), so the compute runs per finding, directly contradicting ground-rule 4 ("compute the plan-state fingerprint once per apply/reconcile pass and reuse it across per-finding records, never recomputing inside the loop") and acceptance criterion "fingerprint compute is hoisted above per-finding loops." The constraint that resolves it: `apply_finding` is the single consumption point of `parse_apply_verdict` shared by six callers, so hoisting is foreclosed unless a precomputed digest is threaded through `apply_finding`'s signature; step 5 (`05-record-escalate-split-outcome-decision`) has the same shape (compute per `escalate_to_split` call, i.e. per structural finding), at lower frequency.
recommendations.suggested_action: reconcile the body with the detail — either scope the hoist rule/criterion to exclude the in-function `apply_finding`/`escalate_to_split` sites (accepting per-finding compute, which the coupled `[apply-verdict-code-fingerprint]` drop makes a cheap plan-file read), or specify threading a once-per-pass digest into `apply_finding` from the apply walk

recommendations.title: Acceptance criterion 1 promises a non-empty `plan_fingerprint` at the two create sites that step 2 cannot deliver. The c
recommendations.body: Acceptance criterion 1 promises a non-empty `plan_fingerprint` at the two create sites that step 2 cannot deliver. The criterion lists "each of the six backfilled call sites (create ×2, code-reveals-split, granularity[completeness], audit-coverage, convergence) carries a non-empty `plan_fingerprint`", and Architecture Part A threads `compute_plan_fingerprint` "into each site that has a plan in hand" including `create.py`. But step 2 (`02-source-pass-fingerprints-create-py-two`) establishes the correct, more-detailed decision: `_review_step_change_types` fires before `write_new_plan` (confirmed at `create.py` — call at ~5634, write at ~5902), so "`plan_fingerprint` (which reads the plan file) has no file to read" and the create sites carry `code_fingerprint` instead. The body oversells; step 2 already scoped it.
recommendations.suggested_action: correct Acceptance criterion 1 and Architecture Part A so the two create sites are documented as carrying a non-empty `code_fingerprint` (not `plan_fingerprint`), because create decisions fire before the plan is written.

recommendations.title: Step 6 (`06-update-backlog-72`) acceptance criterion requires the spike (`.tmp/72-telemetry-linkage.spike.md`) "cited in
recommendations.body: Step 6 (`06-update-backlog-72`) acceptance criterion requires the spike (`.tmp/72-telemetry-linkage.spike.md`) "cited in the Status bullet" of the durable, tracked `BACKLOG.md` #72, but `.tmp/` is gitignored (`.gitignore:29`) transient scratch that routine cleanup (`rm .tmp/<slug>.*`) removes — so the citation dangles the moment the spike is swept, leaving #72's provenance pointer rotted in a file #72 itself insists stay an honest source.
recommendations.suggested_action: have step 6 either promote the spike's cited empirical findings into the backlog entry itself or point at a durable location, rather than mandating a citation to a gitignored transient path.

recommendations.title: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) records a fifth verdict value `UNKNOWN` (normalized from `parse_apply_ver
recommendations.body: Step 4 (`04-record-per-finding-apply-verdict`) records a fifth verdict value `UNKNOWN` (normalized from `parse_apply_verdict` returning `None` when Claude ignored the apply contract), but the plan body's Architecture Part B(2), the acceptance criteria, and the Testing section all enumerate only the four tokens (`APPLIED`/`NOT-APPLICABLE`/`BLOCKED`/`BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL`) — so the contract-violation outcome, the most diagnostically interesting apply result for phase-3 aggregation, has no criterion or test locking it in.
recommendations.suggested_action: add `UNKNOWN` to the enumerated apply-verdict values in the body/acceptance and name its coverage in Testing so the contract-violation case is verified.
